articles.title: From railway tragedy to gov’t change: Serbia’s two-year fight for justice
articles.summary: A timeline of events since the deadly train station collapse in Novi Sad, which led to a change of government in Serbia.
articles.body:
Sunday marks two years since 16 people were killed when a train station canopy collapsed in the Serbian city of Novi Sad.

The accident prompted student-led protests which swiftly evolved into a wider political campaign that brought the Student List opposition movement to power last week.

Here is a timeline of events from the tragedy in Novi Sad on November 1, 2024, to the elections that led to a change of government in Serbia.

November 1, 2024 – The collapse of a concrete canopy on the renovated Novi Sad railway station building kills 14 people at the scene, with three others taken to hospital in critical condition. Two of them later die of their injuries in November 2024 and March 2025, bringing the total number of victims to 16. The tragedy leads to public outrage, raising questions about the quality of the work, lack of transparency in the spending of public money and endemic corruption.

November 5, 2024 – Just four days after the accident, thousands of protesters gather in Novi Sad to demand accountability for those responsible. The protests escalate into clashes with police, with dozens of protesters arrested and City Hall damaged. Observers point to the swift judicial response to the protesters, while the investigation into the accident itself remains stalled.

November 19, 2024 – Opposition MPs, councillors and citizens block the entrance to the court and prosecutor’s office building in Novi Sad for three consecutive days, demanding the release of those arrested and an accelerated investigation into those responsible for the collapse of the canopy. The blockade is marked by daily confrontations with police in riot gear.

November 21, 2024 – After three weeks of public pressure, the higher public prosecutor’s office in Novi Sad announces that 11 people have been arrested in connection with the deaths at the railway station, including former Construction Minister Goran Vesic and other officials.

November 22-25, 2024 – Students and professors come under attack during a memorial service for the victims of the canopy collapse in front of the faculty of dramatic arts of the University of Arts in Belgrade. The incident marks a turning point, prompting students to launch a university sit-in to demand the prosecution of the attackers, the publication of documentation on the railway station’s reconstruction and the release of all detained protesters.

December 11, 2024 – Under strong pressure from months of protests and university blockades, authorities publish part of the documentation on the reconstruction of the railway station. Eight binders containing 195 documents are presented, but students and others dismiss the move as insufficient, demanding full transparency and criminal accountability for the contractors and supervisory institutions.

December 30, 2024 – Prosecutors in Novi Sad officially file an indictment against 13 people on suspicion of committing serious crimes against public security, improper execution of construction works and abuse of office. But higher courts overturn detention orders for Vesic and Serbia Railways Infrastructure’s acting General Director Jelena Tanaskovic, putting them under house arrest. The transparency of the proceedings is further called into question by a dispute over the jurisdiction of the prosecution offices and the transfer of case files.

January 15, 2025 – In addition to the proceedings in Novi Sad for the canopy collapse, the public prosecutor’s office for organised crime in Belgrade officially launches a separate investigation into potential financial fraud, corruption and money laundering during the reconstruction of the railway station. It involves Vesic, former Trade Minister Tomislav Momirovic and 12 other individuals, including managers of construction and supervision companies.

January 28, 2025 – Public outcry erupts after governing party activists attack and cause serious bodily harm to students of the Academy of Arts in Novi Sad. Serbian Prime Minister Milos Vucevic submits his resignation in the government’s biggest political concession to date. However, protests and blockades continue.

March 11, 2025 – Thirteen activists and students are arrested in Novi Sad on the eve of planned large protests in Belgrade, charged with undermining the constitutional order and violent behaviour. The arrests prompt a strong reaction from civil society organisations and citizens, who denounce them as politically motivated and organise protests and road blockades in Novi Sad.

March 15, 2025 – Hundreds of thousands of people demonstrate in Belgrade.

May 28, 2025 – After months of student-led protests and blockades, Novi Sad’s High Court decides to replace prison detention with house arrest for some of the imprisoned activists and students.

June 25, 2025 – With the prosecutor refusing to withdraw the charges of undermining the constitutional order and security services continuing to exert pressure, some of the accused activists leave Serbia for European Union countries, where they continue to draw attention to the situation.

September 9, 2026 – The informal student-led movement morphs into a political force following the announcement of snap parliamentary elections for October. The Student List-Students Win grouping is formed, bringing together students, professors and legal experts.

September 27, 2026 – Longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic resigns as president of Serbia to lead the Serbian Progressive Party-led electoral list. On his last day as president, he pardons all prosecuted students and activists, ending the proceedings for “undermining the constitutional order” and allowing the safe return of activists from exile. The move is widely seen as an attempt to ease social tensions ahead of the election campaign.

October 25, 2025 – Vucic concedes defeat to the Student List in the elections, which saw voter turnout reach its highest level in more than 30 years. Accountability for the Novi Sad railway station tragedy remains a central issue following the announcement of the results.

articles.title: Qatar LNG carrier struck by ‘unidentified objects’ in Gulf
articles.summary: Qatar Gas Transport Company says no injuries or environmental damage.
articles.body:
A Qatari tanker has been hit by “unidentified objects” while sailing in the Gulf, the Qatar Gas Transport Company says, the latest attack on commercial shipping since the US-Israel war on Iran began in February.

The attack on Friday evening struck the liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier Al Mayeda, which belongs to the company, it said in a statement on Sunday.

None of the crew members was injured and no environmental damage was reported, it said.

The statement, published by the Qatar Stock Exchange, said the vessel is currently in a “safe condition, operational” and that the impact of the incident is being assessed.

The Qatar Gas Transport Company supplies Qatari ports and terminals with towage and marine support services.

More than 120 commercial ships have been hit since the start of the war, according to data from the International Maritime Organization and the UK Maritime Trade Operations.

Iran, which closed the Strait of Hormuz early on in the war, has repeatedly warned vessels attempting to pass through the vital waterway without its permission would face “destruction”.

The attacks have increased since the United States reimposed a blockade on Iran’s southern ports in July.

With at least 29 ships hit, October was the worst month of the war, ahead of the 20 attacks recorded in March.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Speaking at the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge vowed to continue the opposition’s fight until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigned, warning that the bloc would “dig him out from the ground if needed”. Kharge vowed that the opposition would continue its agitation until Kumar resigned, accusing him of acting in favour of the ruling BJP.Addressing thousands of supporters and leaders from opposition parties at the ‘Chalo Delhi’ rally, Kharge accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah of attempting to manipulate votes belonging to women, young people and Dalits. He also alleged that PM Modi was trying to divide the country and use central agencies such as the Enforcement Directorate to intimidate the opposition.“PM Modi will go only when you fight strongly,” Kharge told the gathering, urging people to unite against alleged vote theft. He said the INDIA bloc would continue its fight to remove the BJP from power, protect the Constitution and strengthen democracy.RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav also targeted Kumar, accusing him of acting as a “puppet of Modi” and drawing parallels between the political confrontation and the Mahabharata. He described Ramlila Maidan as a Kurukshetra, saying the Opposition had been compelled to fight against what he alleged was electoral manipulation.“While the Ramlila Maidan is traditionally meant for staging the Ramayana, today we have organised a ‘Mahabharata’ for those who steal votes,” Yadav said, invoking Shakuni and the game of dice to allege that the electoral process was being manipulated.The rally was attended by several INDIA bloc leaders, including Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, Trinamool Congress general secretary Abhishek Banerjee, Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren and Telangana chief minister Revanth Reddy.The Opposition parties are protesting alleged irregularities in electoral rolls and the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. They have demanded a halt to the exercise and Kumar’s resignation, alleging that the process has led to large-scale voter omissions.The rally followed heightened security arrangements and traffic restrictions across parts of central Delhi as thousands of supporters gathered in the capital, carrying banners with the slogan ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A Delaware couple kept a fence and garden on disputed land for more than 20 years; new neighbours demanded $30,000 or removal, but an October 30 court ruled the couple owned the strip, including the unfenced planter
articles.summary: A Delaware couple who spent more than two decades looking after a piece of land beside their home have won a court battle against neighbours who wanted
articles.body: A Delaware couple who spent more than two decades looking after a piece of land beside their home have won a court battle against neighbours who wanted them to pay $30,000 or move their fence.According to the judgment, Joseph W C Murray Jr and his wife Danielle, residents of Newark since 1998, faced the demand after a survey revealed that their backyard fence extended into the neighbouring property. On Friday, the Delaware Court of Chancery ruled that the couple had gained ownership of the disputed land through adverse possession, including a garden area that was not enclosed by the fence.The disagreement began when Rade and Zeljka Preradovic purchased the neighbouring house with their son Nikola in December 2022. Before the sale, a property survey identified that the wooden fence separating the two homes crossed into the Preradovics' land by nearly nine feet at one point.The Murrays had bought their house on Pinedale Road in December 1998. At the time, the fence was already standing, along with a stone retaining wall and a raised garden planter. Over the years, they continued looking after the space, replacing sections of fencing, maintaining plants and hiring workers to cut the grass.The problem arose when the new neighbours questioned their right to use the area. Although the fence had stood in roughly the same position for decades, the survey showed that the official property boundary ran elsewhere. The disagreement eventually reached court after attempts to settle it failed.Neighbours offer land for $30,000Shortly after buying the house, the Preradovics informed the Murrays that their fence extended beyond the legal boundary. They gave the couple three options: pay $30,000 to buy the disputed land, shift the fence to the correct boundary or remove it.The Murrays refused to accept those terms. They maintained that the fence had been there for more than 20 years and that they had used the land as part of their home throughout that period.In January 2023, they proposed paying for a survey and the necessary paperwork to change the boundary. Alternatively, they offered $3,000 for a permanent legal right to continue using the land.The neighbours rejected those proposals but remained willing to discuss a sale. By March, they had reduced their asking price to $10,000. They also offered to rent the land to the Murrays for $1,500 a year.The Murrays were prepared to consider the $10,000 purchase, although they wanted the cost of changing the property documents to be shared. The discussions did not produce a lasting agreement.In June 2023, the couple approached the Delaware Court of Chancery, asking it to recognise their rights over the land.How couple had used the land for decadesThe court examined how the disputed area had been used long before the Preradovics bought their house.The previous owners of the Murrays' property, the Burkerts, had lived there from 1980 until 1998. During that period, they replaced an older post-and-rail fence with a wooden privacy fence. The raised planter was already present when they purchased the property.After moving in, the Murrays continued using the enclosed space as their backyard. Danielle maintained flower beds and other plants, while Joseph cut the grass, removed unwanted bamboo and trimmed trees.The couple also made improvements over the years. Parts of the fence were replaced in 2007, and further repairs were carried out in 2022.From May 2007, they paid a landscaper to maintain their yard. His work included cutting the grass beside the planter and keeping vegetation under control.However, the planter itself stood beyond the fence. This became an important issue because the court had to decide whether the couple's long-term use extended to that open section as well.Earlier decision excluded the garden planterThe dispute was heard at trial in October last year. A Magistrate Judge later concluded that the Murrays had established ownership of the land enclosed by their fence.The decision did not extend to the raised planter or the narrow grass strip beside the sidewalk. The Magistrate found that the couple's maintenance of those areas had not been sufficient to establish ownership.Neither side accepted the outcome. The Preradovics argued that the Murrays should not receive any of the disputed land, while the Murrays maintained that the entire area belonged to them.The matter was subsequently reviewed by Chancellor Kathaleen McCormick, who visited the properties in August this year.During the inspection, McCormick observed that the planter outside the fence was connected to the retaining wall inside it. Both structures used the same drainage system, while the surrounding landscaping formed part of the same area.Court on why couple can keep entire stripThe final decision turned on adverse possession, a legal principle under which someone can gain ownership of land by using it in a particular way for a specified period.In Delaware, such a claim requires proof of continuous, open, exclusive and actual possession for at least 20 years, without the legal owner's permission.The court found that the Murrays had met these conditions. Their records, photographs and witness testimony showed that they had cared for the disputed land since moving into the house.Although some plants had occasionally become overgrown, the court did not consider this evidence that the couple had stopped maintaining or claiming the area.It also found that the fence, planter and grass strip had effectively functioned as one part of the Murrays' property.McCormick therefore ruled in their favour over the entire disputed area, reversing the earlier finding that excluded the unfenced sections.The case was returned to the Magistrate to determine the exact boundaries and issue an order formally granting ownership of the land to the Murrays.You use AI every day. articles.title: Bulgarians vote in presidential run-off amid Black Sea tensions
articles.summary: Voters in Bulgaria weigh economic challenges and attacks on ships in a race marked by record low turnout.
articles.body:
Voting is under way in a Bulgarian presidential run-off marked by growing regional security threats and domestic economic concerns.

President Iliana Iotova, 61, led over former caretaker Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov, 50, in the first round but fell short of the 50 percent threshold needed to win. The first round drew record low turnout . Only 23 percent of eligible voters cast a ballot, according to election officials.

Exit ‌polls will be published after voting ends at 8pm (18:00 GMT) on Sunday, with a result expected on Monday.

The presidential vote comes against the backdrop of a series of drone attacks on merchant ships off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast in the past month, which have sparked international condemnation and concerns about the growing reach of Russia’s war ⁠on Ukraine.

About two dozen seafarers are feared dead, and ⁠the strikes have prompted the government to seek help from Bulgaria’s allies to bolster maritime security. On Wednesday, a Greek container ship sank after being hit by sea drones.

Both leading presidential candidates have condemned the attacks. ⁠Prime Minister Rumen Radev, who backs Iotova, said the strikes’ outcome “benefits the Russian Federation”. They have both called for ⁠a diplomatic end to the war in Ukraine.

A victory for ⁠Iotova would make her Bulgaria’s first elected female president. She became acting president in January after Radev resigned to enter and win a parliamentary race on what many political analysts considered a Kremlin-friendly ‌ticket.

Gyurov, who served as caretaker prime minister this year, is supported by pro-Western, reformist parties and has long expressed support for Ukraine.

He signed a security ‌cooperation agreement ‌with Kyiv during his time as premier.

Gyurov said he wants Bulgaria to be a reliable NATO ally able to stand for up its interests with strong diplomacy and a firm position.

A host of right-leaning political figures, among them ex-Prime Minister Boiko Borisov, have expressed support for Gyurov.

The brand’s No. 3 cleanser to create unity and connection was inspired by Becky G and it features notes of bergamot, oud, and vetiver. Not one to miss her family’s white elephant gift exchange, Becky G says a bottle of Patrón Tequila was one of the best presents she’s ever brought. “It was the hot ticket item that everybody was battling it out for, and at the end, people started linking up with other people to trade gifts to get it.” An official partner of the brand, she recently designed an exclusive bottle for the Rainwater Project, which helped bring 200 rainwater harvesting systems to families in Jalisco, Mexico. A fan of buying and gifting things with intention, Becky G is planning on giving friends a bottle from that collection this year because it’s a present that’s connected to something close to her heart. “When I’ve been given things that are for the community and for the culture, it hits me differently and it reminds me that we’re a part of something bigger and it makes me want to do the same,” she says. Patrón silver tequila is an unaged blanco tequila made from 100% Weber Blue Agave. You must be 21+ to purchase and consume. If someone came up to Becky G and asked her for a mid-luxury beauty product to give as a gift, she’d recommend Dezi Skin’s Agua Fresca Moisturizer. “Desi Perkins killed it with Dezi Skin; there’s not one product that I do not love, especially Pore Choices, the new mist she just released. But, the OG Agua Fresca moisturizer is also incredible,” she says. The fragrance-free gel-cream moisturizer is formulated with niacinamide, hyaluronic acid and antioxidants to help give skin a much-needed boost of hydration. It’s lightweight and can be used with all skin types to help target fine lines, dryness and elasticity. Every year, Becky G likes to give her team presents that they can make together. Last year, she bought them a Mexican coffee set from a small cafe in Los Angeles. The kit included the coffeehouse’s signature Café de Olla — a traditional Mexican coffee brewed with ground cinnamon and piloncillo (unrefined Mexican sugar) — and a bag of Oaxaca Reserve beans. “Little thoughtful things like that are super, super fun to put together,” she says. Traditionally, café de olla is made in a clay pot, which imbues the coffee with more flavor. While you can make café de olla in a regular saucepan, you can also purchase an olla for less than $40 on Etsy — just make sure to wash it by hand with warm water and baking soda (or coarse salt) when you’re done. Chemical-based detergents are easily absorbed into the clay and can give your food (and coffee) a soapy taste. One thing about Becky G is she commits to an aesthetic. Each of her family members gets a matching color scheme for the holidays that’s themed to their personalities, which she helps curate on Etsy. “I get down on wrapping presents. That’s the one thing I enjoy,” she says, noting that she’s usually the one going around and saving the tissue paper and unripped bags. “There’s some bags that have been around at my Christmas for eight years now. We can’t just use these once, come on.” As someone who’s always traveling, Becky G loves tin candles, and she thinks they make a great addition to any stocking. “Tin candles help make a room feel a little more custom to your vibe,” she says. “They’re usually a little bit more potent in scent, so you don’t need to leave them [burning] for a very long time.” During the holidays, she opts for scents like apple cinnamon, which she says reminds her of her mom’s house, and pine. One of her go-to candle brands is Soy Latina Candles, a non-toxic soy candle brand that offers scents inspired by the owner’s Latina heritage. Another of Becky G’s go-to stocking stuffer ideas is anything practical that can be kept in a glove box, like individually packed hand wipes, silk hair ties and lip balm. “I be doing too much with the stockings sometimes. I’m like, it’s overflowing at this point,” she says. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a newsletter editor at NBC Selected. I’ve been testing products professionally since 2016 and have previously written for publications like The Cut, Elle, Teen Vogue, Elite Daily and Bustle. To write this article, I interviewed Becky G about her Patrón partnership and her favorite holiday gifts to give and receive. articles.title: Gov Hochul's cameo in Cornell sex-assault documentary casts ‘air of impropriety’ over investigation: attorney

None of the seven men have been criminally charged. Hochul signed an executive order in October assigning New York Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor to investigate the case. In the newly released documentary titled "Instadocs: Jane Doe v. Cornell," Hochul appears around 13 minutes into the film, expressing her own reaction to news surrounding the case. She condemned what she called a "culture" that "has never changed." articles.title: Colombia's 'El Tigre' takes fight to cartels as Trump alliance takes shape
articles.summary: Abelardo de la Espriella claims over 32,000 arrests in ten weeks as Colombia joins Trump's anti-cartel coalition, pivoting away from predecessor's policies.
articles.body: President Abelardo de la Espriella means business when it comes to his war against the cartels. Colombia's new president, known by the nickname of ‘El Tigre’, was voted in on a law and order ticket and so far his actions in fighting the cartels are seemingly paying dividends — not just in Colombia but in Washington too. Recently, he arrived at the Barranquilla police command around the early hours of the morning as 587 police officers and soldiers raided 50 locations across the Caribbean port city and its suburbs in Operation Blindaje 360. A few days earlier, domestic Colombian news outlets had widely publicized a recording intercepted by Colombian police of "Keko", the alleged leader of a gang called "Los del Freseo" boasting that de la Espirella had nothing on him. "The Tiger's got nothing. Let him come out, and we'll put lead in him," Keko allegedly said on the recording. Then, before dawn, Colombia's president had tracked him down and was face to face with him, all caught on tape. According to a video released by his presidential office, El Tigre told Keko the gang leader was "a tough guy on the phone… but the look of the fear on his face matched that of his many victims". The sweep ended with 72 arrests. ANTI-CARTEL HARDLINER CHANNELS TRUMP IN BID TO END COLOMBIA'S LEFTIST ERA IN PIVOTAL ELECTION The theatrics played to a large audience who long argued that former leftist Gustavo Petros’s policy of pursuing engagement with drug traffickers and through conversation and peace talks had left Colombia more vulnerable to organized crime and further articulation between Colombian and Venezuelan cartels that had been dominating the space left by the power vacuum which emerged from effective law-enforcement control. His government is also seeking to reverse former President Gustavo Petro’s "total peace" policy, which pursued negotiations with several armed organizations. Before taking office, de la Espriella announced that he would dismantle key elements of the policy and reactivate arrest warrants against members of illegal armed groups. Nearly three months into his term, the 48-year-old lawyer has scrapped his leftist predecessor's "total peace" talks, ordered every armed group treated as a terrorist organization and claims more than 32,000 arrests. He is doing it arm in arm with Washington. A dual U.S.-Colombian citizen who lived in Miami before running for president, he has brought Colombia into President Donald Trump's anti-cartel coalition. Last month, he personally handed a guerrilla boss accused of supplying Mexico's Sinaloa Cartel to DEA agents with his hands and feet shackled. The prisoner, Geovany Andrés Rojas, alias "Araña," is alleged to have led the "Comandos de la Frontera" dissidents and now faces narco-terrorism charges in Southern California. "The option of dialogue is completely exhausted," de la Espriella told troops after his Aug. 7 inauguration. In an Oct. 12 address, he put the tally at 32,503 arrests, 33 ringleaders taken out of action and 679 drug-production sites destroyed or disabled. He has signed more than 100 extradition orders, including five for former armed-group peace negotiators wanted in the U.S. whose handovers the previous government had frozen. ‘DONROE’ DOCTRINE AND CONSERVATIVE VICTORIES SQUEEZE CARTELS IN LATIN AMERICA The offensive reaches deep into the countryside, where conflict monitor ACLED counted August as the deadliest month for clashes between security forces and armed groups since it began tracking Colombia in 2018. In late August he warned FARC dissident chief Iván Mordisco: "When you least expect it, a bomb is going to fall on you." Two days later, he walked among the bagged bodies of 23 suspected dissidents at an army base in Guaviare, and troops killed the top commander of a paramilitary-rooted trafficking group in La Guajira. Colombia became the 19th member of Trump's Shield of the Americas coalition in August, and War Secretary Pete Hegseth said Bogotá had authorized "joint military operations to destroy terrorists and terror networks domestically." The administration has pledged $1 billion in security aid, pending congressional approval, and Marine Gen. Francis Donovan, head of U.S. Southern Command, has toured Colombian bases. However, speaking on-camera to Fox News Digital, Colombian Vice President José Manuel Restrepo said while his country is embracing President Donald Trump’s push for a new security alliance across the Western Hemisphere, he drew a clear line on the role American forces would play inside Colombia, saying Colombian troops — not U.S. forces — will carry out operations against the country’s armed groups. PENTAGON SENDS HUNDREDS OF ARMY TROOPS TO LATIN AMERICA FOR TRAINING AS DRUG-TRAFFICKING CAMPAIGN EXPANDS According to Benjamin Gedan, a senior fellow and director of the Latin America Program at the Stimson Center in Washington who previously served as a South America Director in the White House, the last few years were an outlier: "For decades, the United States and Colombia closely cooperated to fight guerrillas and organized crime. Plan Colombia was celebrated by both Republicans and Democrats. The Colombian military is well-trained and battle-tested. Renewed close cooperation between Bogotá and Washington is a cornerstone of the renewed U.S. focus on security in Latin America," he said. "Still, flashy military strikes on criminal targets will not answer the mail. These groups are well-armed, well-funded, and thrive in regions with little state presence. Images of criminals in body bags may give the impression of forward progress after the failed strategy of Colombia’s last leader, much as videos of exploding speedboats have become the calling card of the Shield of the Americas. In both cases, a more sophisticated strategy is needed to deal lasting blows to criminal groups," Gedan argued. CRIME, KIDNAPPINGS AND DRONE ATTACKS FLAGGED IN US WARNING FOR BORDER REGION Oscar Palma, a professor of Security Studies at the University of Rosario in Bogotá, said it is still a little too early to assess the change in policies and affirm they will be fruitful within the Colombian context. "Beyond the policing acts themselves, there is the subjective feeling of security with debates within Colombian society on whether this open war strategy brings more or less security to the population. Many argue that the gangs are acting now more forcefully to defend their territories and business deals, while others believe that a strong police presence will eventually lead to less organized crime." Palma said there is a false dichotomy between having to choose all-out war or dialogue in order to achieve peace with groups such as the FARC and other gang leaders: "It is a fiction that you will come to zero combatants simply pursuing one strategy or the other—all-out war will never zero down those combating in the FARC and organized crime just as peace talks, especially if carried out in a misguided policy such as the one led by [Gustavo] Petros, will achieve real results." He said, "A better example is the strategy carried out by President [Juán Manuel] Santos during the dealings with the FARC, which led to a much safer Colombia: there were talks, but those were part of a bigger strategy of also fighting these groups with arms and bringing them to justice," he added. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "There is a wave of freedom, a wave of democracy, a wave of free market… There is a new momentum for the region and we have to take advantage of that momentum. That's what I said to President Trump," Restrepo told Fox News Digital. "If we want to keep and preserve democracy in the region, the Shield of the Americas is going to be the best opportunity to do it."

articles.title: Mediators continue US-Iran negotiations amid war rhetoric: What we know
articles.summary: Trump says latest talks ‘going fine’; Iranian leaders say they favour diplomacy but are ready to respond to US attacks.
articles.body:
Iranian officials have been speaking with Qatari mediators about a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, in the latest effort to find a diplomatic path out of the US-Israel war on Iran that has caused a serious global energy crisis.

But even amid signs of diplomatic progress, officials from both sides say they are ready for renewed military escalation .

President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly suggested the United States could attack Iran after the November 3 midterm elections, said the latest negotiations were “going fine”, but added that the US still had several Iranian targets to “take care of”.

Meanwhile, Araghchi has also said Iran’s military was more prepared than ever for renewed war, while the country’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, threatened Iran would use “new weaponry” in response to any future attack.

Here’s what we know about the latest diplomatic efforts and the sharp rhetoric from both sides, and what it could mean for what lies ahead:

Araghchi said on Saturday that an Iranian delegation, including one of his aides, travelled to Doha to meet Qatari mediators. Earlier, Qatari officials also travelled to Tehran for consultations.

The latest discussions in Doha centred on a plan that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a global energy chokepoint, within two days and restart peace talks with the US, provided Washington meets a set of demands from Tehran, Araghchi told Al Jazeera.

Those demands include the lifting of recently imposed US sanctions, the reinstatement of oil waivers granted in June, a reduction in the US military presence in the region, recognition of new shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz designated by Iran and Oman, and an end to the conflict on all fronts, including Israel’s attacks on Lebanon, said Araghchi.

Qatari and Pakistani mediators were “continuing consultations regarding our conditions”, said the top Iranian diplomat.

Pakistan has been mediating between the US and Iran, with its army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, visiting Tehran several times as part of the diplomatic efforts to end the war. Doha and Islamabad played key roles in the signing of the June memorandum of understanding (MoU) that collapsed in August.

Iran’s Rezaei said the US had “indicated its readiness” to accept its conditions, although Washington has not confirmed this.

On the US side, Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed Qatar-led talks were ongoing, but said he was not aware of a timeframe for them.

“There are multiple talks. Talks have actually never stopped,” said Rubio. “If there is a diplomatic solution, we would be open to it.”

Why has Iran noted a change in the US’s ‘tone’?

The renewed diplomatic activity comes after US Vice President JD Vance sent a letter earlier this week to Rezaei, reportedly seeking to gauge the prospects of restarting negotiations and averting another round of military escalation.

Rezaei confirmed on Saturday that he had read the letter, whose tone he said had “completely changed” compared with earlier correspondence from Trump.

Araghchi also said he had studied Vance’s letter, which he described positively.

“The American side’s attempt to open the door to dialogue and understanding more broadly is a positive step,” Araghchi told Al Jazeera.

However, he warned, “If Washington’s goal in sending this letter is to stir up discord, it would be yet another mistake to add to its previous ones.”

What has Iran said about prospects for peace and war?

Iranian officials have said they are open to new peace talks if the US meets their conditions, but also ready to act more aggressively in any new military confrontation.

“I know that our armed forces are more prepared for war than any time before, and we are ready for any scenario,” Araghchi told Al Jazeera.

In the event of any new military threat from the US or Israel, Iran’s response would be “immediate” and “without geographical limitations”, according to a statement by Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.

Khamenei ordered commanders to update Iran’s target list to include “all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy”.

Rezaei told Al Jazeera that Iran would use “new weaponry” in its response to any future attacks. He also said Iran’s government was weighing a change to its “nuclear doctrine”, which currently includes a ban on nuclear weapons.

Iran’s nuclear programme has been a major point of contention in the conflict with the US, and Trump has repeatedly said Iran must never be allowed to acquire a nuclear weapon. Tehran insists its nuclear programme is for civilian purposes.

The US president has sent mixed signals about the status of peace talks. On Saturday, he said negotiations were “going fine” but added that they were “not very reliable”.

He also said the US military still needed to “take care of” several Iranian sites, singling out a suspected underground nuclear complex known as Pickaxe Mountain .

Trump added that the US could achieve its military objectives “very quickly” and was not in a hurry.

Previously, he threatened to renew attacks that would “finish off” Iran, while the US has reportedly warned its Gulf allies to prepare for a short, high-intensity round of conflict after the midterm elections.

Rubio said Trump had not yet decided on whether to carry out new strikes, but warned the US “can achieve military objectives if we seek to”.

How could Israel play into the calculation?

Israel, which joined the US in initiating the war against Iran in February, is preparing for another round of potential conflict right after the US midterm elections, according to a senior Israeli official cited by Israel’s Ynet News site.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said Israel has a “historic, one-time opportunity … to remove the Iranian threat once and for all”. While Netanyahu’s coalition lost its parliamentary majority in recent legislative elections , the 77-year-old leader remains in office as caretaker until a new government is formed.

Andreas Krieg, an associate professor of security studies at King’s College London, told Al Jazeera that Netanyahu’s threats complicate Iran’s calculus because Tehran fears “even a nuclear agreement with Washington may not end the threat of another Israeli attack”.

Brigadier-General Yadollah Javani, the deputy for political affairs of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, said Iranian forces are operating on the assumption that the US or Israel could strike at any moment.

What explains the parallel diplomatic efforts and war rhetoric?

Hamidreza Azizi, a senior Iran analyst with the Crisis Group, said Tehran is pursuing diplomacy while also “attempting to redefine” the military implications of another potential conflict.

“For now, diplomacy and military preparations are proceeding simultaneously,” he wrote in a post on X. “The emerging Iranian position seems to be that an agreement remains possible, but another war would be fought under different rules and on a much wider battlefield.”

He added, “Whether Washington takes these warnings as credible deterrence or further escalatory threats could significantly influence what happens next.”

Krieg said the November 3 elections give Iran an incentive to delay concessions to deny Trump a diplomatic victory. But that calculus could change afterwards when he has fewer domestic political restraints on military action.

“We could therefore reach a situation where Iran becomes more willing to compromise precisely when Washington becomes more willing to strike,” said Krieg.

articles.title: Thousands rally in New Delhi to demand India’s election chief resign
articles.summary: Hundreds of police, some carrying batons and shields, are deployed around the rally site.
articles.body:
Thousands of protesters have taken to the streets in India’s capital, New Delhi, to demand the resignation of the election chief over changes to voter lists that opposition parties say favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party.

Indian National Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi led Sunday’s demonstration, the latest in more than a month of protests challenging the revision of electoral rolls and the conduct of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Opposition parties alleged the exercise, which removed more than 130 million names from voter lists, disproportionately affected Muslims and other minorities considered unlikely to support Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said voters whose names were wrongly removed may register again.

The BJP has accused opposition parties of undermining democracy by challenging legitimate electoral procedures. India’s next general election is due in 2029.

Officials ramped up security measures and announced traffic diversions before demonstrators marched from central New Delhi towards the historic Ramlila Maidan ground.

Hundreds of police, some carrying batons and shields, were deployed around the rally site alongside riot-control vehicles. Demonstrators waved Indian and party flags as opposition leaders travelled in an open-top jeep.

Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda dismissed the demonstration as a “carefully orchestrated drama”.

“What is unfolding today at Ramlila Maidan is not an act of respect for democracy,” he told the ANI news agency. “It is a calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy, all in the name of democracy.”

Opposition parties, student organisations and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party have staged near-daily demonstrations since late September, calling for Kumar to step down.

The protests began after Kumar’s two deputies raised concerns about revisions to voter lists, registration procedures and digital systems.

Analysts described the demonstrations and growing support for the opposition as Modi’s most serious political crisis since he took office in 2014.

articles.title: Riots loot stores in Frankfurt as European youths protest living costs and military service
articles.summary: Rioters looted stores and set fires to barricades in Frankfurt on Saturday as protests across Germany demanded lower living costs and better education.
articles.body: Rioters looted stores and set fires to barricades in Frankfurt on Saturday as protests across Germany demanded lower living costs and better education. Tens of thousands of people across more than 30 cities took to the streets, including in the capital Berlin and financial hub Frankfurt, in protests organized by the campaign group Gen Z regelt (Gen Z takes charge). The activists demand spending on schools, climate protection and housing, and are against plans to return to mandatory military service. But the largely peaceful protests, which coincided with Halloween and came weeks after some of the worst rioting in decades erupted in neighboring France, turned violent in some areas. “In ⁠the city centre, windows have been smashed at several shops,” Frankfurt police said on X. “Molotov cocktails are also being thrown at the emergency services. We urge all bystanders to avoid the ​city center or to leave the area.” In Hamburg, some barricades were set on fire. Some businesses had boarded up their windows and doors in preparation for the protests. “We are here today to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion,” Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina ​Friedrich said in Berlin on Saturday. “What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service and we ​are in favor of a fairer distribution of the burden.” Official numbers Saturday afternoon suggested turnout was below the 182,000 participants that organizers initially expected. The protests took place alongside many others in Europe. France, Italy, Serbia and Spain have seen protests against the cost of living, among other causes. In France, student protests about the state of education last month evolved into wider demonstrations about the cost of living and social security. As the demonstrations began Saturday afternoon in Paris, protesters were pictured holding a banner that read: “We do not need tear gas for our future to be blurry.” Videos vetted by NBC News show large crowds and fires burning in Marseille. Roman Poseck, interior minister for the state of Hesse, which includes Frankfurt, warned Germans against using protests in France as an example ahead of Saturday’s protests. “We all have those images from France in our minds — looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers,” he said. “France must not be held up as a model in this regard.” France’s Interior Ministry said turnout stood at 320,000 on Saturday. In Italy, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s far-right government also said it would deploy 500 army troops alongside the police in Milan until the end of the year after groups of masked protesters looted stores in the fashion capital and elsewhere and threw projectiles at police earlier this month. Tens of thousands of people again took to the streets of Rome on Friday and other cities and towns across the country. The demonstrations were largely peaceful, but an NBC News crew saw police use a water cannon on protesters and groups of police charging to disperse protesters. In Serbia, student-led activism also helped unseat the country’s long-time leader at the ballot box. Meanwhile, police in Portugal early Sunday forcibly cleared a tent camp set up in Lisbon by activists protesting against high housing costs. Hundreds of protesters shielding the tent camp were dispersed by police using shields and some baton charges, the Reuters news agency reported. While the protests across the continent have drawn comparisons for their timing, Andrew Barclay, a politics lecturer at the University of Sheffield, said it was important to focus on their differences. The French protests have involved “hundreds of thousands taking to the streets over many weeks, and at least initially centered on specific grievances about education funding,” he told NBC News. While protests elsewhere may have taken inspiration form the French, he said, “their scale so far hasn’t been as large, and whilst the state of education continues to be a common theme, the issues being protested has ballooned to include a much larger number of complaints.” Similarly, Barclay said the protests in Germany and France were unlikely to lead to a direct change in governance as they did in Serbia. “Often protests, even quite large ones, don’t capture that level of support elsewhere in the country,” he said. “I would be very cautious about comparing what we have seen in Serbia, where students and others have organized to oppose state corruption, to the sorts of protests that we are seeing elsewhere.”

articles.title: California Governor Gavin Newsom warns federal judges of possible ballot seizures ahead of US midterm elections
articles.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom warns federal judges of potential ballot seizures by the Trump administration ahead of the 2026 midterm elections amidst ongoing legal disputes over voter records.
articles.body: California Governor Gavin Newsom has asked federal judges to remain alert to possible attempts by the Trump administration to seize election ballots and related materials ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections, amid an ongoing legal dispute over federal demands for voter records.In a letter to federal judges on Saturday, Newsom said he was concerned that federal agents could seek search warrants to take possession of ballots before election results are officially certified.“Given the United States Department of Justice’s persistence in advancing this baseless theory of criminal liability, I have grave concerns federal agents will seek search warrants to seize ballots and ballot materials before the election results are certified,” Newsom wrote.He argued that such warrants could interfere with California's election process, including the counting of votes and certification of results.The warning follows a series of legal setbacks for the Trump administration in its efforts to obtain California's election records as part of an investigation into alleged noncitizen voter registration. On Friday, a US appeals court rejected the administration's latest attempt to block the state from counting votes allegedly cast by noncitizens.The dispute centres on the Justice Department's claim that more than 20,000 noncitizens are registered to vote in California. However, state officials and election experts have questioned the accuracy of the federal government's list.The Justice Department has not disclosed how many people identified in its records have actually cast ballots. California officials have described the information as unreliable, arguing that complying with federal demands could result in eligible voters being wrongly removed from the electoral process.A separate federal court ruling has also restricted the administration's approach. A judge ordered the Justice Department to stop threatening criminal prosecution against state and local election officials who refuse to comply with its election-related demands.The dispute has raised questions over the federal government's authority in administering elections. The US Constitution gives states responsibility for conducting elections, while the Trump administration has pursued access to voter records through its investigation into alleged noncitizen registration.You use AI every day. articles.title: Plymouth aquarium shark that helped 'dispel myths' dies
articles.summary: Staff at Plymouth's aquarium pay tribute to a sand tiger shark believed to be almost 30 years old.
articles.body:
A sand tiger shark that had been at an aquarium since its opening almost 30 years ago has died.

Staff at the National Marine Aquarium (NMA) in Plymouth said they had noticed changes in the behaviour and condition of Howard, also known as Howie, and she was put to sleep after not responding to medical intervention.

She was initially living in the Great Barrier Reef habitat before moving to the Atlantic Ocean habitat where she grew to 9ft (2.7m) long.

The team said the shark was believed to have been almost 30 years old and acted as an "incredible ambassador, helping to dispel many of the myths around this critically endangered species".

Staff said: "The team at the NMA are very sad to lose such a presence from the aquarium.

"A huge thank you to our valued visitors for your support and understanding at this time.

"Rest assured, our beautiful sand tigers, Ushaka and Mandela, can still be seen in our Atlantic Ocean habitat."

articles.title: Matt Robertson wins record $1.25 million fishing prize, declares 'trailer trash for life'
articles.summary: Matt Robertson won $1.25 million at the world bass fishing championship on Old Hickory Lake but plans to stay in his trailer and buy more.
articles.body: NASHVILLE — Matt Robertson just became $1.25 million richer. But don't expect the Kentucky bass fishing pro to pack up and move into a mansion anytime soon. "We ain't moving out the trailer, baby. Trailer trash for life!" Robertson declared during a Saturday evening news conference after winning World Bass Enterprises' inaugural The Champions tournament on Old Hickory Lake in Tennessee. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS The Bassmaster Elite pro backed up a week's worth of trash talk by bringing 20 pounds, 2 ounces of bass to the scales on Championship Saturday, claiming the largest first-place prize in professional bass fishing history. And despite all that confidence, even Robertson seemed a little overwhelmed by the moment. "Dude, it's freaking insane. I don't think it's really hit me yet," he said. Robertson, of Kuttawa, Kentucky, dominated the first two days of competition, then delivered another monster bag Saturday after the weights reset to zero. Pake South finished second with 13 pounds, 7 ounces, taking home $500,000, while Wesley Strader earned $300,000 for third place. The historic tournament brought together top anglers from the Bassmaster Elite Series and Major League Fishing's Bass Pro Tour, along with two amateur qualifiers, to compete for a record $3.25 million purse. But for Robertson, the payday is about much more than the money. A millionaire who's staying in his trailer Robertson might not be upgrading his own home, but he already knows where some of that $1.25 million is going. His wife is getting a new vehicle. And he's planning to buy a couple more trailers. Before the final weigh-in, Robertson told OutKick OutDoors that he'd been eyeing two trailers for sale near his home, one priced around $60,000 and the other around $80,000. "I'm for sure buying a couple more trailers," he said. "They're bought, and my wife, she gets her new ride." MATT ROBERTSON HAULS IN 20-POUND BAG TO LEAD THE CHAMPIONS AFTER DAY 1 ON OLD HICKORY LAKE And after securing the championship, he doubled down on those plans. "I hate to tell anybody, but them things are sold," he joked. Behind Robertson's larger-than-life personality, however, is a man who hasn't forgotten where he came from. "I didn't grow up with much," he explained during his post-victory press conference. "I worked so much paycheck to paycheck ... I went through real struggles in life." Those experiences, he said, helped prepare him for the pressure of competing for life-changing money. Robertson admitted that the money will drastically change his life, but he insisted he wasn't particularly nervous about the stakes. In fact, when OutKick OutDoors asked him what winning would mean before the results were officially announced, he had something else on his mind. "I want that damn trophy. It's what I want," he said. "Everybody talking about the 1.25. Like, I want the money too, but I want to get my hands on that trophy." A honey hole, a navigation lock and an unlikely friendship While Robertson's victory might have looked easy from the leaderboard, it took some unconventional strategy to get there. Rather than fishing the main lake, he traveled through the navigation lock at Old Hickory Dam to target smallmouth bass in the tailwater below the dam. Robertson discovered his productive fishing area during practice and made the gamble that the bigger fish would be there when it mattered. "If I hadn't found that spot, I wouldn't have won this thing," Robertson said. The strategy certainly paid off. Robertson caught the tournament's only 20-pound bag on Thursday, then added another strong day Friday to secure the top qualifying position for Saturday's championship. But his honey hole wasn't exactly a secret. MLF pro Ron Nelson had also discovered productive water below the dam, and the two anglers spent much of the tournament fishing in close proximity. The two were among just a handful of competitors who ventured below the dam. In fact, Nelson deliberately avoided casting into the area where Robertson had been catching his fish, despite the enormous money at stake. And Robertson noticed. "Never knew Ron before this week. Got to know him real well, and dude, there is not another person in the world with as much integrity as him," Robertson told OutKick OutDoors during Saturday's weigh-in. "Anybody else fishing for this kind of money, he saw where I was catching a lot of fish, and he never came in on me." As water levels and currents shifted, the two eventually ended up sharing the productive area. But tournament rules prohibited them from discussing how many fish they had caught, creating an unusual dilemma. Robertson said he had no idea Nelson was struggling to fill his limit and felt terrible afterward. "If I'd knew Ron only had two ... I wouldn't even have pulled up down there," he said. "I feel awful about it." Robertson had been hoping they could both walk away with enormous paydays. "I was wanting us to win $1.75 million from down there," he said. Nelson, who ultimately finished sixth and earned $75,000, had equally kind words for his new friend. "Matt's a heck of a dude," Nelson told OutKick OutDoors. "I don't know him, but I got a new friend now, I guess." Nelson explained that changing currents had made it difficult to relocate the school of smallmouth he'd found the previous day. And he believed Robertson would have given him more room had he known how badly Nelson needed a few additional bites. "If he knows I'd needed a couple bites, he'd have probably slid over," Nelson said. The mutual respect was especially fitting for a tournament that brought together competitors from rival professional fishing circuits. Robertson and Nelson had never met before The Champions. Three days later, they'd walked away with substantial paychecks and a new friendship. 'The Super Bowl of bass fishing' Robertson was also quick to credit his faith and a little help from the lock operators for his historic victory. He recalled learning that the navigation lock was undergoing maintenance early in the tournament, threatening to keep him from reaching the area where he'd found his fish. Knowing how much his strategy depended on getting through, he said he prayed for the lock to reopen. When he checked his phone, he discovered the lockmaster had already tried calling him twice. The lock was open, and the operators were waiting for him. "From that moment, I was stressing before that," Robertson recalled. "And after that, I just ... gave it all to Him and let it go." Once on the water, Robertson relied on his familiarity with the Tennessee River and its navigation locks to adjust to changing conditions. He caught his winning fish using a small swimbait on a jighead. The victory capped a tournament that also saw Bassmaster's Team Stars defeat MLF's Team Stripes for the team championship, giving the inaugural event both individual and team bragging rights. Robertson had nothing but praise for WBE and CEO Brian Bird, saying the organizers had paid attention to both the big details and the small ones. "This is the Super Bowl of bass fishing. I don't care what anybody says," Robertson declared. And while he can now claim the sport's richest championship prize, Robertson says he doesn't plan to change who he is. A new vehicle for his wife? Absolutely. A couple more trailers? Already on the shopping list. But moving out of his own? Not a chance. articles.body: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has instructed the country's armed forces to deliver an immediate and forceful response to any renewed US or Israeli attack, warning that Tehran would decide when and under what conditions hostilities would end.In a meeting with the country's top three military commanders, Khamenei called for maximum combat readiness and said any threat must be met with an effective response, without geographical limitations, according to a statement from his office reported by Axios and Iranian state media outlet Tehran Times."If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it will be the Islamic Republic of Iran's Armed Forces and the Iranian nation that determine when and under what conditions those hostilities will end," Khamenei said.The meeting marked the first publicly disclosed gathering between Khamenei and all three senior military commanders since the war began, Axios reported. He called for strengthening military intelligence, expanding indigenous defence capabilities and incorporating emerging technologies into the country's security infrastructure.The commanders, including Armed Forces Chief of Staff Major General Ali Abdollahi, Army Commander Major General Amir Hatami and Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps chief Major General Ahmad Vahidi, briefed Khamenei on military preparedness along the Persian Gulf coastline, the Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf of Oman and Iran's northwestern and southeastern borders.They also reported a several-fold increase in the production of ammunition, reconnaissance equipment and support and combat weapons, according to Tehran Times.The warning was reinforced by Iran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei, who threatened "devastating blows" against any aggressor, saying Tehran would use "new weaponry" if attacked. articles.body: US President Donald Trump has said Brazilian politician Flavio Bolsonaro can remain in the United States for as long as he wishes, signalling that tensions between Washington and Brasilia could continue despite recent diplomatic contact between the two countries.Trump made the remarks while speaking to reporters at a Halloween party at his Mar-a-Lago club in Florida on Saturday. He is also facing two federal money-laundering investigations, while police in Brazil had considered him a flight risk.Bolsonaro's stay in US raises questionsBolsonaro entered the United States under humanitarian parole, Reuters had previously reported. The immigration status is generally granted for a limited period, typically one year.Trump's latest remarks suggest he is willing to let Bolsonaro remain in the country beyond that period. However, the US President said he had no plans to meet the Brazilian politician, who has described himself as Brazil's rightful leader.A US official and another person familiar with the matter told Reuters that Trump currently has no plans to support Bolsonaro's political ambitions, despite allowing him to enter the United States.US and Brazil maintain diplomatic contactThe comments came as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio held talks with Brazilian Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira on the sidelines of a Group of 20 meeting in Atlanta on Saturday.Rubio said the two had spoken and were expected to meet again in France next month during a G7 foreign ministers' summit. articles.body: A bullet missed Brandon Boudreaux’s head by inches when a gunman opened fire on him outside his Arizona home in 2019. The failed assassination exposed a murder-for-hire plot involving Lori Vallow Daybell. Prosecutors said she recruited her brother, Alex Cox, to kill Boudreaux, who was in the midst of a contentious divorce from Vallow’s niece, Melani Pawlowski. Now, Boudreaux is telling his side of the story. On Oct. 2, 2019, Cox allegedly fired from a parked Jeep Wrangler as Boudreaux pulled his Tesla into the driveway at his Gilbert home. Boudreaux saw the vehicle’s rear window open moments before the shooter fired. A bullet struck Boudreaux’s driver’s-side door, shattering the window. ARIZONA JURY FINDS 'CULT MOM' LORI VALLOW GUILTY OF CONSPIRING TO MURDER LATE HUSBAND Although police identified Cox as the suspected shooter shortly after the attack, he died in December 2019 without facing charges. An Arizona jury convicted Vallow, known as the "cult mom," in June 2025 of conspiring to kill Boudreaux. Two months earlier, another jury convicted her of conspiring to murder her estranged husband, Charles Vallow, whom Cox shot and killed in July 2019. The Arizona convictions followed Vallow’s 2023 Idaho trial. Jurors found her guilty of murdering her two children, Tylee Ryan, 16, and Joshua "JJ" Vallow, 7, and conspiring to murder Tammy Daybell, the former wife of her husband, Chad Daybell. Jurors also convicted her of grand theft for collecting her children’s Social Security benefits. Sharing his story Boudreaux is telling his story in his new book, "Unthinkable." He initially wrote the book privately for his four children. He wanted them to have a broader account of the ordeal and understand his decisions. "I'm sure I made some mistakes," Boudreaux told Fox News Digital. "If they need some closure, if they need to understand better... my goal was to give them all the information." He also hoped to demonstrate how his faith anchored him, while giving his children the freedom to choose their own spiritual path. "I want them to understand their dad and maybe in understanding their dad and why he made the choices he did, maybe they'll understand themselves better," he said. "They all encouraged me," he said. "They said they thought it was good enough and there was enough in there that people would be interested in." Still, Boudreaux waited until the criminal proceedings advanced before speaking publicly, purposely avoiding the release of information that could interfere with the investigations. "I needed to go on the stand with a defense attorney," he said. "I just felt more comfortable waiting and making sure that I let that process go first." "Now that it feels like it's most likely done, it was something that I always kind of intended to share my perspective on." Divorce and shooting During Vallow’s Idaho murder trial, Boudreaux testified that his marriage to Pawlowski collapsed in 2019 as she grew closer to Vallow. The couple filed for divorce in July 2019. They later fought over custody of their children. The filing also claimed Chad Daybell told Pawlowski something must happen to Boudreaux to advance his spirit and the Lord’s plan. Boudreaux, who remarried in 2020, said the shooting, his divorce and the lingering fear that someone was still after him left him struggling to trust others. articles.title: Iran and US explore diplomacy amid rising threats of war
articles.summary: Iran says could reopen Hormuz in shorter period if conditions met, as Trump says US still has targets to ‘take care of’.
articles.body:
Tehran, Iran – Ongoing contacts through mediators have provided a potential diplomatic opening between Iran and the United States, even as both sides express readiness for renewed military escalation.

After two days of Qatari-mediated talks, Iranian authorities have signalled that a deal remains possible provided that their demands are tangibly implemented. At the same time, they have doubled down on a willingness to expand attacks or even launch preemptive strikes if they deem war is inevitable.

“We are prepared for all scenarios,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Al Jazeera on Saturday. “We have upgraded our weaponry, addressed our vulnerabilities, and tested new arms. Our forces are at the highest level of readiness.”

His comments came as US President Donald Trump said on Saturday the talks were going “fine” but added that Iranian authorities were not “reliable”.

The Republican leader, who ordered attacks alongside Israel against Iran on February 28, has repeatedly raised prospects of once more hitting the country’s civilian infrastructure. In recent weeks, he has suggested that an attack could potentially take place after the November 3 midterm elections in the US.

“We still have to take care of, I would say, one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes,” Trump told reporters at a Halloween party at his Mar-a-Lago Club in Florida about further bombing Iran’s nuclear facilities.

The mediated talks in Tehran on Friday, and then in Qatar on Saturday, appear to have produced a new tangible result by shortening the period after which Iran’s proposal to partly reopen the Strait of Hormuz can be enforced.

Tehran had previously offered seven days, but that has now come down to two, Araghchi said in his interview with Al Jazeera.

Negar Mortazavi, a senior fellow with the Center for International Policy, said there are “indications” of US interest in a negotiated settlement, citing the continuing Qatar-mediated talks and US Vice President JD Vance’s recent outreach .

“However, Iran is seeking a series of concessions while the United States insists on progress on Iran’s nuclear programme before concessions are made,” she told Al Jazeera.

“Therefore the central difficulty is sequencing and leverage. Each side wants the other to act first.”

Araghchi’s two-day offer indicates some flexibility over sequencing that could also allow both sides to claim an initial diplomatic achievement without immediately resolving their fundamental disagreements, according to Hamidreza Azizi, a senior Iran analyst at the International Crisis Group.

“However, the military statements show the limits of this opening. Iran appears increasingly determined to prevent a repetition of previous scenarios in which negotiations or temporary ceasefires were followed by renewed military conflict,” he wrote on social media. “From Tehran’s perspective, the objective is to make another attack so costly and unpredictable that Washington would have to reconsider the option altogether.”

As the talks were ongoing on Saturday, the office of Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said he had a meeting earlier with top military commanders to demand “maximum deterrence” through preparedness for an immediate response “without geographical restriction” to any threat.

Targets would include “tangible and intangible” US and Israeli assets, Khamenei said. Iranian authorities have previously said if Iran’s civilian infrastructure is attacked again, seabed cables and infrastructure across the region could also become targets.

After Khamenei’s statement, commanders of the general staff of the armed forces, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the traditional army separately expressed readiness to launch missile, drone and other attacks in case of an escalation of conflict.

State media on Sunday also aired footage of missiles and drones being taken out of massive underground storage sites and deployed during the eight months of war so far.

The authorities also signalled that they expect more potential attacks from the US and Israel, including against Iran’s power grid.

Gholamreza Jalali, commander of the National Organization for Passive Defense, said during a speech on Sunday that they have identified 14 sectors most dependent on electricity that would need support if the war restarts, without naming any.

“Adopting preventive measures in the area of passive defence for the electricity grid is a fundamental principle that all authorities must follow up in their capacities,” he said, adding that officials were considering “network islanding” practices to create different segments that would not all be simultaneously affected by potential bombing.

In and around the Strait of Hormuz, vessels continue to be attacked if they refuse to coordinate with the Persian Gulf Strait Authority, the entity set up by Iranian authorities to enforce control and sovereignty in the critical waterway.

At least four tankers were identified as being hit on Friday and Saturday, although not all attacks are reported by vessels and monitors. According to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations, a vessel carrying liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) was struck by three Iranian projectiles on Saturday about 40 nautical miles (74km) south of Iran’s Lavan Island, deep into the Gulf.

Transit in the strait and surrounding waterways will not return to normal unless the US takes steps towards Iran’s conditions, security chief Mohsen Rezaei told state television during an interview on Saturday night.

For the sequencing to work, he said Tehran wants the US to lift its naval blockade that has halted oil exports and the majority of Iran’s trade, which used to be facilitated through its southern ports. The US must also issue waivers for oil sanctions, unfreeze Iran’s assets abroad, stop fighting on all regional fronts, including Lebanon, and recognise a bilateral Iran-Oman arrangement for Hormuz.

Rezaei said he has yet to respond to a letter addressed to him by Vance, although he said the missive indicated a “change in tone” that he described as “positive”.

Mostafa Najafi, a Tehran-based political analyst said to be linked with Rezaei, said if the conditions are not met, the letter is likely to go unanswered and negotiations – including on Iran’s nuclear programme – will not enter a higher level.

“It is unclear how willing Washington is to accept these demands. It is clear that not recognising rights emphasised by Iran will lead to the failure of the negotiations,” he wrote on X.

The US has also doubled down on the effectiveness of its Operation Economic Outcast involving the blockade, sanctions and pressure on overland trade and aviation.

A report by the US Treasury to inform Trump’s decision-making, which was publicised by news outlet Axios, said no new oil had been loaded onto tankers at Iran’s terminals since August 25. It also showed overseas crude deliveries were down, while Iran’s year-on-year inflation neared 90 percent in September and the national currency continued to dwindle.

The report said Iran’s economy was “crippled” by the combined measures, but did not argue that it was close to collapsing.

articles.title: Nita Ambani marks birthday with foundation stone ceremony for 5,000-person care facility
articles.summary: Nita Ambani marked her birthday on Sunday by laying the foundation stone for a proposed 100-acre care township in Karjat, Maharashtra.
articles.body: Nita Ambani marked her birthday on Sunday by laying the foundation stone for a proposed 100-acre care township in Karjat, Maharashtra. The project, Nita Mukesh Ambani Anant Ashray, is envisioned as a lifelong home for more than 5,000 people, including orphaned children, senior citizens and people with developmental disabilities.Mukesh Ambani and members of the Ambani family attended the bhumi pujan and groundbreaking ceremony near Mumbai. The township, being established by Reliance Foundation, will be developed as a permanent, not-for-profit institution in phases. It is planned as a community with residential homes, healthcare facilities, schools, rehabilitation services and opportunities for education, work and recreation.Nita Ambani said the project was a step towards creating “a loving home for people with disabilities, children who need a home and seniors who seek care and comfort”. She said the township would combine medical support with the warmth of family life and give residents opportunities to learn, work, make friends and participate in festivals and celebrations.According to the plans shared by Reliance Foundation, the township will support a wider community of approximately 15,000 people, including residents, caregivers, medical professionals, support staff and their families.The proposed facility will comprise eight residential villages, each named after a sacred river of India. Residents will live in small, family-style homes supported by house parents and caregivers. Their rooms will be designed to offer familiarity and personal belonging, with residents encouraged to personalise their living spaces.The project will include a specialised hospital offering developmental medicine, epilepsy care, special-needs dentistry, palliative care and other medical services. Rehabilitation facilities for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and hydrotherapy are also planned.Other proposed amenities include a temple, gardens, farms, playgrounds, workshops, cafés and inclusive sports and recreational facilities. An animal companionship farm is expected to be developed with expertise from Vantara.The township will also offer vocational training and employment opportunities through facilities such as a bakery, café and craft studios. A dedicated training academy for disability-care professionals, a hospice wing and a garden of remembrance are also part of the plans.The initiative is expected to have an impact beyond the township. Around 1,000 people from nearby areas are expected to access therapy, education and employment opportunities, while respite-care facilities, mobile medical clinics and outreach programmes will support families in neighbouring districts.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Gautam Gambhir said there is no word for fear in his dictionary as India's tour rolls on.

He wants eight or nine days of red-ball preparation rather than the three on offer.

India play five ODIs and two Tests in New Zealand between November 4 and December 1.

Gautam Gambhir ready to 'take the bullet' as India's New Zealand tour rolls on

India wrapped up the T20I leg in Hamilton on Sunday with a series win and two defeats, and have four days before the ODIs begin in Auckland. Gautam Gambhir was asked about carrying that load across three formats and did not reach for any excuses.

"I am ready to take the bullet… it gets tough. I am also human but I am up for the challenge and that's my job," the head coach told reporters .

He put it more bluntly when the subject turned to the pressure of the job itself, borrowing a Hindi word to make the point.

"There is no word like 'dar' in my dictionary and directory," Gambhir said, before turning the attention back to his players and what they had managed in the opening week.

"The way our boys handled pressure, winning first game after 15-hour flight and one practice session was commendable," he added .

Gambhir wants more preparation time before the Tests

The one area where he did push back was the calendar. India landed in New Zealand with a single practice session before the opening T20I, and face a similar squeeze before the Tests, with the fifth ODI in Tauranga on November 15 and the first Test in Wellington starting four days later.

"Planning is done at BCCI level. Prioritising is important. Every match for country is important," Gambhir said . "Three day prep for red ball is not important. 8-9 days will be good."

He made the same argument about the T20I leg, pointing out that the squad arrived from the West Indies series with one day to adjust and most of the group had never played in New Zealand before. Different weather, different dimensions, different conditions, as he put it.

The BCCI has already split the squads to ease some of that, with a separate group staying back to prepare with the red ball while the ODIs are played.

The Cricket News Opinion: Gambhir is right about the preparation

The scheduling complaint has merit. India arrived after a 15-hour flight, had one session, and still won the first three T20Is, which rather proves his point about what the players managed, not what the calendar allowed.

The red-ball argument is the more serious one. India were whitewashed 3-0 at home by New Zealand in 2024 and have not won a Test series in the country since 2009, and four days between a day-night ODI in Tauranga and the first morning at the Basin Reserve is not an ideal time for preparation.

articles.title: U.S. warned Russia of possible Moscow terror attack, FSB says
articles.summary: Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) ​said it had received information from ‌the United States through established partner channels about preparations for a terrorist attack ​in Moscow and was taking ​appropriate measures.
articles.body: Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) ​said it had received information from ‌the United States through established partner channels about preparations for a terrorist attack ​in Moscow and was taking ​appropriate measures. The U.S. Embassy in Moscow ⁠said separately it was “aware of ​a credible threat of a mass casualty ​event” on Saturday at Moscow’s Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve and that the U.S. government was ​coordinating with Russian authorities. The Tsaritsyno ​Museum Reserve, a palace museum and park complex ‌south ⁠of Moscow, was temporarily closed on Saturday and access to the park is currently restricted, the RIA news agency ​reported, ​citing Russian ⁠law enforcement agencies. Russian tabloid Baza reported that the venue was evacuated toward the end of an organ concert, which was cut short with about ten minutes left in the program. A separate concert dedicated to the folk traditions of the North Caucasus region was subsequently canceled, the outlet reported. In March 2024, the U.S. Embassy warned ​that extremists had imminent plans ​for ⁠an attack in Moscow. Days later, gunmen attacked the Crocus City Hall ⁠concert ​venue outside Moscow, killing ​more than 140 people.
